title: Human GeoClick replay: a memory hook for every placement
opening: He hides the redundant controls with the eye icons. Now he puts the state names and the lessons' memory hooks together.
closing: Forty-nine out of forty-nine on the first try, with zero mistakes. He has connected the state names, their shapes and the facts from the regional lessons.

hooks.Florida: He places Florida, the peninsula pointing south. Its Everglades are a slow-moving river of grass.
hooks.Arizona: Arizona is Grand Canyon country, directly below Utah. That canyon is the memory hook.
hooks.Indiana: He places Indiana between Ohio and Illinois. The Indianapolis 500, first raced in 1911, fixes the name.
hooks.Kentucky: Kentucky sits above Tennessee. Its Mammoth Cave is the world's longest known cave system.
hooks.Missouri: Missouri goes below Iowa. St Louis and the Gateway Arch are its westward-expansion hook.
hooks.New Mexico: New Mexico belongs below Colorado. Trinity and Los Alamos provide the historical memory hook.
hooks.Oklahoma: He places Oklahoma above Texas. Its western panhandle and the Sooner nickname recall the lesson.
hooks.Tennessee: Tennessee is the long strip below Kentucky. Its name recalls the Cherokee town of Tanasi.
hooks.Arkansas: Arkansas sits above Louisiana. At Crater of Diamonds, visitors can keep the diamonds they find.
hooks.Maine: Maine is the wooded northeastern corner. Nearly nine-tenths of its land is covered by forest.
hooks.Idaho: Idaho's narrow panhandle reaches toward Canada. Hells Canyon marks its border with Oregon.
hooks.Mississippi: He places Mississippi west of Alabama: the great river and the Delta blues are the hooks.
hooks.Michigan: Michigan has two main peninsulas. The Mackinac Bridge joins them across the straits.
hooks.Minnesota: Minnesota goes above Iowa. Lake Itasca, where the Mississippi begins, is the memory hook.
hooks.Colorado: Colorado sits above New Mexico. Even its lowest point exceeds eighteen other states' highest points.
hooks.Montana: Montana is mountain country in the west, with Glacier National Park as its landscape hook.
hooks.Louisiana: Louisiana belongs below Arkansas. Its name honours Louis the Fourteenth; the Mississippi reaches the coast here.
hooks.South Carolina: South Carolina sits below North Carolina. Charleston's Fort Sumter recalls the Civil War's beginning in 1861.
hooks.Ohio: Ohio reaches Lake Erie. Dayton, where the Wright brothers developed their aircraft, supplies the memory hook.
hooks.South Dakota: South Dakota is the lower Dakota. Its Black Hills and Mount Rushmore recall the lesson.
hooks.New Jersey: New Jersey hugs the Atlantic below New York. Edison's Menlo Park laboratory is the memory hook.
hooks.Pennsylvania: Pennsylvania means Penn's woods. Philadelphia connects it with the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution.
hooks.New York: New York stretches inland from the coast. The Erie Canal linked the Hudson River and the Great Lakes.
hooks.California: He places California, the long Pacific state. Its name came from Queen Calafia's fictional island.
hooks.Maryland: Maryland wraps around Chesapeake Bay. Fort McHenry connects it with The Star-Spangled Banner.
hooks.North Dakota: North Dakota sits above South Dakota. Both became states on the same day in 1889.
hooks.Alabama: Alabama reaches the Gulf. Huntsville's Rocket City connects it with the Apollo programme.
hooks.Texas: Texas goes below Oklahoma. Its independent republic began in 1836, before U.S. statehood in 1845.
hooks.Nevada: Nevada fits California's diagonal border. Its snow-covered name recalls the Sierra Nevada.
hooks.Connecticut: Connecticut sits below Massachusetts and west of Rhode Island. Its name recalls a long tidal river.
hooks.Massachusetts: Massachusetts belongs above Connecticut. Harvard, founded in 1636, is the historical memory hook.
hooks.Illinois: Illinois has a silent final s. Chicago's 1871 fire and rebuilding connect it with early skyscrapers.
hooks.Iowa: Iowa sits above Missouri, between river borders. Its corn-growing landscape is the memory hook.
hooks.Georgia: Georgia belongs above Florida. Its name honours King George; Martin Luther King was born in Atlanta.
hooks.Delaware: Delaware is the small strip east of Maryland. First State recalls its 1787 ratification of the Constitution.
hooks.Kansas: Kansas belongs below Nebraska. Topeka recalls Brown versus Board of Education and the 1954 school-segregation ruling.
hooks.Nebraska: Nebraska sits above Kansas. Flat water recalls the Platte River; its legislature has just one house.
hooks.Wisconsin: Wisconsin lies west of Lake Michigan. America's Dairyland supplies the cheese-making memory hook.
hooks.Washington: Washington sits above Oregon. George Washington's name and Mount St Helens in 1980 are the hooks.
hooks.Oregon: Oregon sits between Washington and California. Crater Lake is the deepest lake in the United States.
hooks.New Hampshire: New Hampshire is east of Vermont. The Old Man of the Mountain's collapse in 2003 supplies the memory hook.
hooks.Vermont: Vermont belongs west of New Hampshire. Green Mountain State recalls the French origin of its name.
hooks.West Virginia: West Virginia is a separate mountain state. It split from Virginia during the Civil War in 1863.
hooks.Virginia: Virginia belongs below Maryland. Elizabeth the First's name and eight Virginia-born presidents are the memory hooks.
hooks.North Carolina: North Carolina reaches from mountains to the Outer Banks. Near Kitty Hawk, the Wright brothers flew in 1903.
hooks.District of Columbia: He places D.C., the capital district on the Potomac, far from Washington State on the Pacific.
hooks.Rhode Island: Rhode Island is the tiny coastal state below Massachusetts and east of Connecticut: the smallest U.S. state.
hooks.Wyoming: Wyoming sits below Montana. Yellowstone and women's voting rights in 1869 are its memory hooks.
hooks.Utah: Utah belongs above Arizona. The Ute people give it its name; the Great Salt Lake is its landmark.
